claims.text: Rockstar's page sets the game in 'Vice City, USA' within the state of Leonida.
Rockstar's page shows only the year 2026 (release and Newswire dates) and gives no in-story year.
claims.uncertainty: Absence on the official pages read; Rockstar may announce a year later.

claims.text: In GTA V, players trade stocks through the in-game internet.
GTA V has two stock exchanges, LCN and BAWSAQ; guides say LCN moves with the player's own actions and BAWSAQ with the community of online players.
claims.uncertainty: Narrated as 'Fans say'. Two exchanges: Prima, TechSpot, GTA BOOM. LCN driven by own actions: Prima, Digital Citizen. BAWSAQ driven by other players: Prima and a reader reply on TechSpot only. Nothing official from Rockstar; nothing for VI.

claims.text: Al Capone was convicted of income-tax evasion in October 1931 and sentenced to 11 years in federal prison.
claims.uncertainty: Verdict 17 October (NARA exhibit, Wikipedia, HISTORY) or 18 October (FBI, Prologue text); sentencing 'a week later' (Wikipedia), 'a month later' (Prologue) or 24 November (FBI). The narration says only 'October 1931' and 'eleven years'.

claims.text: Capone died at his home on Palm Island, Miami Beach, Florida, on 25 January 1947.
claims.uncertainty: FBI: he resided on Palm Island until his death; Wikipedia: died in his home.

claims.text: In 1930 the Chicago Crime Commission's widely publicised Public Enemies list put Capone first ('Public Enemy Number One').
claims.uncertainty: Month differs: NARA gives 23 April 1930, Wikipedia places it in March 1930. Narrate only 'in 1930'.

claims.text: Capone sponsored a soup kitchen in Chicago during the Depression (a NARA photograph dates one to February 1931).
claims.uncertainty: The opening date is not established; narrate 'during the Depression'.

claims.text: IRS investigator Frank J. Wilson found ledgers with the line 'Frank paid $17,500 for Al', a key link in the tax case against Capone.
claims.uncertainty: Amount and wording: Wikipedia and Grant Thornton; HISTORY confirms the ledgers without the amount. That Irey sent Wilson in May 1930 and the bookkeeper's name (Leslie Shumway) are Wikipedia only. Indictment counts differ between sources: do not give a number.

claims.text: In The Godfather, Genco Pura Olive Oil Company is the main legal front of Vito Corleone's syndicate.
claims.uncertainty: Fictional canon. The name 'Genco Pura' is in Wikipedia and Vegetarian Times; AFI confirms the olive-oil business as a legitimate cover without the name.

claims.text: In The Godfather, Vito refuses Sollozzo's offer to back the narcotics (heroin) trade because the politicians and judges he controls would turn against him.
claims.uncertainty: Fictional canon. AFI words the reason as his political influence; Wikipedia and Filmsite name judges and politicians.

claims.text: In The Godfather, Vito dies of a heart attack in his garden while playing with his grandson (Wikipedia dates it 29 July 1955).
claims.uncertainty: Fictional canon. The death scene is corroborated; the YEAR is not: Wikipedia says 1955, Filmsite 1954, AFI gives none. 'In 1955' is single-source and contradicted; say 'in the mid-1950s' or drop the year.

claims.text: A phone camera that makes every act public plays the role the newsreel and press played for Capone.
claims.uncertainty: Our inference from Capone's 1930 Public Enemy listing and the soup kitchen; no source makes this comparison.

claims.text: Tommy Shelby (Peaky Blinders, set in Birmingham; story years 1929 and 1933-34): elected MP, feeds false information to the informant Billy Grade, but also plans the assassination of Oswald Mosley, murders the Barwell family and trades in opium.
claims.uncertainty: Fictional canon. MP: Wikipedia, NME. Mosley assassination plan: Wikipedia, NME, Den of Geek. False information to Billy Grade: Wikipedia, Looper (Looper credits 'the Peaky Blinders'). Barwell murders and opium: Wikipedia only. Election year and constituency not confirmed. 'Wins by data with no gunfire' is our inference, not canon.

claims.text: Rockstar's main GTA VI page shows nothing official for VI about a wanted system, money, crypto, laundering or legacy GTA V brands (LifeInvader, Bleeter, BAWSAQ, LCN).
claims.uncertainty: Absence on one page, not a denial; the characters and places once listed here are now named on the Only in Leonida page (C-51..C-55). What VI does with these systems is a guess.

claims.text: Our rating of Capone (opinion): Brutality 5, Adaptability 1, Tech-Savviness 1, Intimidation 4, Chaos Management 2; after the test, Intimidation 2. Reasons: public reputation for violence, a business and fame tied to one city and to paper records (the ledger, C-21).
claims.uncertainty: Our opinion, said as 'our rating'; the star values are the creator's and cannot be verified; the reasons cite the sources listed.

claims.text: Our rating of Vito Corleone, film-era Don (opinion): Brutality 2, Adaptability 2, Tech-Savviness 1, Influence/Networking 5, Strategy 4; after the test, Influence 3 outside his circle. Reasons: power from favours, judges and politicians (C-24), the olive-oil front (C-23).
claims.uncertainty: Our opinion, said as 'our rating'; the star values are the creator's and cannot be verified; the reasons cite the sources listed.

claims.text: Our rating of the invented Yakuza boss Haruto Mizuno (opinion, invented character): Brutality 4, Adaptability 4, Tech-Savviness 4, Discipline 5, Chaos Management 2; after the test, Discipline 4. His play is the GTA V stock-market way (C-11).
claims.uncertainty: Our opinion, said as 'our rating'; the star values are the creator's and cannot be verified; the reasons cite the sources listed. The character, his name and his corporate play are invented by us: no real person or group; no Japanese-law claim is made.

claims.text: Our rating of Tommy Shelby, 1930s (opinion): Brutality 3, Adaptability 5, Tech-Savviness 5, Intelligence/Strategy 5, Influence 4; after the test, Strategy 4. Reasons: information and politics but also violence and opium (C-28); Tech-Savviness is relative to his era.
claims.uncertainty: Our opinion, said as 'our rating'; the star values are the creator's and cannot be verified; the reasons cite the sources listed.

claims.text: The scenario is invented: four bosses from different eras placed in Leonida's Vice City; Rockstar gives no in-game year (C-04), so the year is our assumption.
claims.uncertainty: Said plainly in the narration; the source shows only that no in-story year is given.

claims.text: The 'Florida-style' comic inserts are fully invented: no real incident, person or headline.
claims.uncertainty: Our own statement about our invention; the source is cited only for the Florida-style setting the inserts parody.

claims.text: In GTA V, committing crimes draws a police response shown as a wanted level in stars.
claims.uncertainty: The claim map's 'rises when the police witness a crime' is NOT supported: GTA BOOM says unmodded GTA V police respond to any crime without a witness ('omniscient'). Narrate 'when you commit a crime', not 'when the police see you'.

claims.uncertainty: The page names but does not describe Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia or Mount Kalaga.
